title: DOEE — LIHEAP FY2027
excerpt: FY2027 LIHEAP applications are open. DOEE says the regular one-time benefit may range from $250 to $1,800 depending on household size, income, heating source, and dwelling. This is not an individual benefit estimate. Apply online from October 20, 2026, or by mail to Department of Energy & Environment, Attn: Utility Affordability Administration, 1200 First Street NE, 5th Floor, Washington DC 20002. As of November 18, 2026, DOEE says it has shut down scheduling in-person appointments for FY2027 due to high volume; emergency walk-ins are not accepted. Call 311 or (202) 737-4404 for assistance and current instructions. DOEE alone accepts and processes LIHEAP applications. Documentation listed: unexpired government photo ID for applicant, Social Security cards for household members, proof of current household income, recent utility bills, and utility disconnection documentation if applicable. Do not send these documents to BillHelp DC. Emergency assistance involves additional conditions and must be handled by DOEE.

title: DOEE — Utility Discount Program FY2027
excerpt: FY2027 Utility Discount Program (UDP) applications are open. DOEE states utility bills must be in the applicant's name and the applicant must meet the program-specific income guidelines. DOEE lists potential electric discounts up to $475 per year with electric heat or $300 without electric heat, and gas discounts up to $276 during the winter season. These are upper limits, not individual estimates. FY27 income guidelines are published as an image on the DOEE webpage and are NOT transcribed or verified in this beta. Therefore the assistant must not calculate or decide UDP eligibility. For help call 311 or (202) 737-4404. The webpage also notes that in-person appointment scheduling was shut down as of November 18, 2026.

title: DOEE — Utility Affordability Programs
excerpt: DOEE lists LIHEAP for energy bills, UDP for utility discounts, CRIAC for DC Water impervious area charge discounts, Weatherization Assistance Program, and Solar for All. These programs have different eligibility criteria. Residents should consult the linked program pages and DOEE for current requirements. DOEE lists government-issued photo ID, Social Security cards for household members, proof of current income, and recent utility bills as application documents.
